regressions: Original live code failed all four new cases: rapid release lost before 220ms settle, portrait fold folio [2,1] instead of [2,2], VI and EN touch navigated instead of previewing.

Intermediate native capture recorded a 45px flick: move at 22.5ms, release at 90.4ms; renderer work diluted total-duration velocity below threshold. Recent movement velocity and final pointer sample now drive touch recognition.

A renderer reset during Reduced Motion change could drop a release when semantic commit belonged to the renderer. Reader now owns every accepted touch release even if animation disappears; desktop mouse settle remains.
Compatibility-click suppression now excludes separate mouse/keyboard clicks on coarse devices; pinned previews retain internal scrolling and close/outside/Escape behavior.
scope: Reader touch commit/ordered chapter-restoration queue, BookFlip portrait reverse and per-instance CSS cache, Tooltips pinned touch preview. No book/storage/schema/backend changes.

visual.noteScreenshot: Initial capture can show the 120ms entrance; final live confirmation waits for full opacity.

limitations: Chromium mouse, synthetic pointer and native CDP touch; no physical Android/iOS, Safari or field FPS calibration.
Lifecycle tests use DOM events, not a claim of actual OS freezing; speech tests mock browser speech.
